Good morning guys on a Saturday !

Went through two concall transcripts, Bluestone Jewellery and Urban Company.

The key highlights from the company's concall transcripts 

BLUESTONE JEWELLERY 

1. New initiatives : Men's and Kid's exclusive jewellery stores.

2. FY27 & FY28 is going to see significant drop in FOCO stores.

3. We are currently in a high growth phase setting up new stores.

4. 20% new store addition on a current base of 340 stores ( COCO + FOCO ) for FY27 and FY28.

5. Minimum 14 cr to 15 cr revenue peer store at peak utilisation.

6. 20% CAGR growth on distribution for several years going forward.

7. SSSG in Q4FY26 of around 34% is not something new , FY20 SSSG was around 30%. Q2 & Q3 of FY25 where good grew the sharpest , in those quarters SSSG's had been the lowest. We perform well when gold is stable.

8. A&P cost to remain at around 6% ( not going overboard on brand building until the distribution is in place )

URBAN COMPANY 

> Highest consol NTV growth in 15 quarters. Crossed 10 million orders in a single quarter for the 1st time.

> 4 points capture where UC stands today.

1. Core is accelerating with structurally improving margins. Growth of 26% in Q4 in India Consumer Services with adj EBIDTA margins expanding to 3.3% from 1.6% a year ago. This business was loss making in FY24.

2. International is scaling rapidly and profitable. UAE and Singapore delivered 84% NTV growth in Q4 to 211 cr. For full year International NTV grew 75% to 700 cr and the business turned adjusted EBIDTA positive. This business is now 4 times the scale it was 4 years ago.

3. Native is on a clear path to profitability. NTV grew 67% in Q4 to 89 cr and 345 cr for the full year - up 122%. EBIDTA loss narrowed from 39 cr in FY25 to 31 cr in FY26. Margins improving from -25.1% to -8.9% of NTV in a single year. 75% of the customers whose devices have hit the first replacement cycle are renewing through UC.

4. Insta help is our most significant investment today and we are leaning in. A business that did not exist at the start of FY26 delivered 2.7 million orders and ₹40 cr of NTV in Q4 with match alone crossing 1.1 million orders. The ₹119 cr adj EBIDTA loss reflects the cost of building a market : Consumer acquisition, network density subsidies and supply onboarding. We are investigating to win and we intent to stay ahead.

> Consol adj EBIDTA break even by Q3FY28 and ₹1,000 cr by FY31.

> India Consumer Services has been accelerating from the last 3 quarters. Wait and watch for the next 3-4 quarters before calling it a long term trend. 

> We don't worry about competition too much. Our eyes are on the customer and the service professional and we are planning to win.

> Penetrating deeper markets in the established micro markets is the current focus rather than adding new markets. Cost to serve has to work out well before adding new markets.

> Not worried about the size of the TAM of Insta help , we want to win and win big. Attack it aggressively and win it.

The interesting thing about markets is that sometimes the ugliest quarter on paper becomes the exact quarter where the story changes 📉➡️📈

Sammaan Capital just reported a massive FY26 loss of more than ₹7,100 crore and most people looking at headlines tomorrow morning will probably call it a disaster. But if you actually go through the details and especially listen carefully to the concall, this quarter feels less like a collapse and more like a company deciding to clean every single wound in one shot instead of hiding the pain for years.

They sold bad loans to ARCs, took huge write offs, added extra provisions and basically dumped every legacy issue into Q4. The result after all this destruction is honestly fascinating 👀

✅ Gross NPA at 0%
✅ Net NPA at 0%
✅ Fresh strategic promoter in IHC with a committed $1 billion investment
✅ AA+ ratings from all major agencies within just 50 days
✅ Lower expected borrowing costs
✅ Return to growth guidance for FY27
That is a completely different company from the one the market was pricing a year ago.
What stood out to me most during the concall was the confidence in the tone. This no longer sounded like a management team trying to defend survival. It sounded like a team already thinking about scale 🚀
Gagan Banga repeatedly emphasized that this business is not about asset management this business is about liability management and honestly that may become the biggest driver of the rerating story from here. Because once funding costs structurally fall for an NBFC the entire earnings engine changes.
Another line from the concall that stayed with me was
The chapter of the legacy book stands firmly closed once and for all

And that single line probably captures the entire market debate going forward.

For years Sammaan was treated like a stressed lender carrying baggage from the past. Now the market has to slowly process whether this becomes a recapitalized retail NBFC backed by deep global capital with a cleaned up balance sheet and room to grow again.

And psychology matters a lot here. Markets usually move ahead of reported earnings. By the time profits visibly recover the rerating often already happens. What institutions will now focus on is not the FY26 loss itself but what comes after it.

Management is guiding for more than ₹30,000 crore disbursals, ₹1,400 crore PAT in FY27, improving margins, lower funding costs, dividend payouts returning and even AI driven operational efficiencies over the next few years. Suddenly the conversation changes from can they survive to how fast can profitability normalize. That shift in narrative is huge.

And the interesting part is who was listening carefully on that call 👀

BlackRock
Barclays
Deutsche Bank
ICICI Bank
MUFG
Emkay

These are serious institutions tracking whether this is just another temporary cleanup story or the beginning of a genuine long term rerating cycle.

Of course execution risks remain and credibility will have to be rebuilt quarter by quarter. The market will not blindly trust management overnight. But this genuinely feels like one of those rare quarters where reported numbers look terrible while the forward story quietly improves underneath 📊

Sometimes the biggest rallies begin exactly when the financial statements still look the worst.
